title: Power Automate: share Process license capacity across cloud flows with flow groups
summary: The cost rating describes indirect overhead only, although using a flow group requires a paid Power Automate Process capacity licence. The documented limits, maker navigation and Dataverse creation endpoint are supported; the monitoring checklist also lacks a corresponding controls-table row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Flow groups share a Power Automate Process license's capacity across multiple cloud flows.
claims.quote: A flow group lets you share the capacity of a Power Automate Process license across multiple cloud flows, instead of dedicating a license to each flow separately.

claims.claim: A flow group can contain up to 25 cloud flows.
claims.quote: A group can contain up to 25 solution-aware cloud flows.

claims.claim: Learn supplies no completion date for the regional flow-group rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: "flow groups" rollout finish date regions. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/create-flow-group and /power-automate/flow-groups; the rollout note names July 2026 as the start and says it continues across regions, without a finish date.

claims.claim: Cost is low, meaning indirect cost only, because the required Process licence is assumed already bought.
claims.quote: Power Automate Process: Capacity license (paid). The briefing says licensing.model: add-on but cost: low; the standard defines low as indirect cost only and medium as add-on licences for a subset of users, or predictable consumption.
claims.fix: Set cost to medium. Replace the cost rationale with: "Medium. Flow groups require paid Power Automate Process capacity. Existing available capacity can be reused; otherwise Process licences must be purchased, with admin and maker time in addition."
